body.heading: Where in the world is Republic of the Congo?
paragraphs: Republic of the Congo is a country in Middle Africa, which is part of Africa.

body.heading: The capital city
paragraphs: The capital of Republic of the Congo is Brazzaville.

body.heading: Words you might hear
paragraphs: People in Republic of the Congo speak French and Lingala.

body.heading: Money in your pocket
paragraphs: The money of Republic of the Congo is the Central African CFA franc. The CFA franc is shared with neighbouring countries, so the same money works across the region.

body.heading: How big is Republic of the Congo?
paragraphs: Republic of the Congo covers about 342,000 square kilometres of land and inland water. That makes it about three times the size of Benin.

body.heading: Two places we'd love to visit
paragraphs: Odzala-Kokoua is an ancient rainforest where western lowland gorillas, forest elephants and colourful birds live among giant trees and swampy clearings.
Brazzaville sits on the mighty Congo River, facing Kinshasa across the water — the two closest capital cities in the world. River boats and markets make it lively to explore.

body.heading: Think and talk
paragraphs: 1. Find Republic of the Congo on a map or globe. Which continent is it on — and can you name a country that sits next to it?
2. Spark and Mango can visit only ONE of the two places in this article. Which should they choose — and what would you pack for the trip?
